sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (true/false, match the columns, fill in the blanks or give reasons).

questions.q: In your laundry room you find four laundry powders A, B, C and D with these functions. Powder A: makes white clothes appear brighter when dried in sunlight. Powder B: eliminates yellow tints when added just before the final rinse. Powder C: safely removes stains from both silk and cotton. Powder D: gives cotton clothes a crisp, stiff finish and helps them resist dirt. Identify these powders.
questions.answer: A: optical brightening agent (OBA). B: blue (fabric whitener). C: hydrogen peroxide (a universal bleach). D: starch (stiffening agent).

questions.q: Give a material or reagent for each stain. (a) Tea or coffee on cotton (b) Blood stain (c) Grass stain (old) (d) Paan stain.
questions.answer: (a) Borax or boiling water. (b) Cold salted water. (c) Methylated spirit. (d) A paste of onion.

questions.q: State True or False. (a) Woollen clothes should be soaked before washing. (b) White clothes should be dried in shade. (c) Optical brightening agents are colourless dyes. (d) Silks should be washed by kneading and squeezing.
questions.answer: (a) False: they felt when soaked. (b) False: whites are dried in the sun. (c) True. (d) True.

questions.q: Give one word. (a) A collective name for white petrol, methylated spirit and benzene (b) A chemical used as a fabric whitener (c) A cleanser produced synthetically from chemicals (d) A natural oxidising bleach.
questions.answer: (a) Volatile (dry cleaning) solvents. (b) Blue. (c) Syndet. (d) Sunlight.

questions.q: You find a grass stain on your white cotton shirt. What should you do first and why?
questions.answer: Wash it with soap and cold water first if it is fresh. If it is old, dip the stain in methylated spirit because it dissolves the chlorophyll stain.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Your friend spilled fresh curry on her white cotton kurta. Suggest two immediate steps she should take to remove the stain.
questions.answer: Apply talcum powder on the fresh stain and leave it for a few hours, then brush it off. Wash with hot water and soap and dry in the sun.

questions.q: Give one reason each for the statements. (i) Woollen clothes should not be soaked before washing. (ii) Clothes should not be stored when damp. (iii) Blood stains should be removed with cold water.
questions.answer: (i) Soaking leads to felting of wool. (ii) Moisture causes mildew. (iii) Hot water coagulates blood proteins and fixes the stain.

questions.q: Why is vinegar sometimes added to the final rinse for silks? Why are woollens packed in newspapers?
questions.answer: Vinegar removes soap traces and keeps silk bright. Newspaper ink repels moths.

questions.q: What is laundering? Name its steps in order (any five).
questions.answer: Laundering is washing, drying and finishing of clothes. The steps are mending, stain removal, sorting, soaking, washing, rinsing, starching or bluing, drying and ironing.

questions.q: Name two differences between a soap and a syndet.
questions.answer: A soap is made from natural oil or fat; a syndet is made synthetically from chemicals. Syndets work in hard water and leave no deposits; soaps foam well only in soft water.

questions.q: What are auxiliaries in laundering? Give two examples.
questions.answer: Products other than cleansers that give a good finish are auxiliaries. Blues and optical brightening agents are examples.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain the precautions to be taken while removing stains (three points).
questions.answer: (i) Remove the stain when fresh and identify the fabric and the stain. (ii) Wash first with cold water (hot coagulates blood and egg) and use mild chemicals, trying them on a small portion first. (iii) Wash with soap solution at the end to remove chemicals and dry in the sun.

questions.q: Distinguish between oxidising and reducing bleaches (three points).
questions.answer: (i) Oxidising bleaches have an almost permanent effect and are used on cotton and linen (sunlight, Javelle water, hydrogen peroxide). (ii) Reducing bleaches are milder and used on wool and silk (sodium hydrosulphite). (iii) Wool and silk bleached with reducing bleaches may turn yellow again in air.

questions.q: Explain the precautions for storing clothes (three points).
questions.answer: (i) Brush clothes and sun and air them before storing. (ii) Never store damp or very dirty clothes. (iii) Protect against insects with neem, camphor or moth balls and pack woollens in newspaper.

questions.q: Explain the different methods of washing and the fabrics suited to each.
questions.answer: (i) Friction washing (by hand, brush or beating) for strong cottons. (ii) Suction washing for heavy pile fabrics such as towels. (iii) Kneading and squeezing for delicate silk, wool and rayon, and machine washing for large loads.

questions.q: How will you wash woollen clothes? (three points)
questions.answer: (i) Do not soak them; use lukewarm water and mild liquid soap or reetha solution (not for whites). (ii) Use light pressure and kneading and squeezing. (iii) Rinse well and dry flat in shade; press with a damp muslin.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain the steps in laundering of clothes.
questions.answer: (i) Mending tears and loose buttons and removing stains before washing. (ii) Sorting by fibre, colour and degree of dirt. (iii) Soaking to loosen dirt (not for woollens or non-fast colours). (iv) Washing with soap or syndet by a suitable method, then rinsing till all soap goes. (v) Starching and bluing as required. (vi) Drying (whites in sun, coloured in shade, woollens flat) and ironing according to the fabric.
